question: How can one without a guide not be blind and pathless?
premises: a man is needed as guide
without such a man one is blind
without guidance one goes without path
inference: absence of a human guide leaves one spiritually blind and directionless
uncertainties: whether naraḥ means guru or any guide
plain_english: Whose guide is not present, he is blind; how would he not be a pathless goer?
